=== STAKEHOLDERS ===
[{'type': 'text', 'text': "# Stakeholder Identification Report: LIC Market-Driven System\n\n**Prepared by:** Requirements Analysis Team, Retinodes Software Company  \n**Client:** Life Insurance Corporation (LIC)  \n**Project:** LIC Market-Driven System (MDS)  \n**Document Version:** 1.0  \n\n---\n\n## 1. Executive Summary\n\nAs part of Retinodes Software Company’s Requirements Engineering initiative, this document establishes the comprehensive stakeholder matrix for the proposed **LIC Market-Driven System (MDS)**. \n\nBecause MDS is a greenfield, market-facing solution aimed at digitizing agent-insurer workflows and enabling customizable/consolidated insurance packages, identifying all internal, external, and project-level stakeholders is essential. This identification forms the foundation for requirements elicitation, conflict resolution, prioritization, and feasibility analysis.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Stakeholder Taxonomy & Detailed Profiles\n\nStakeholders have been categorized into four primary groups: **Internal LIC Business Stakeholders**, **External End-Users**, **Governance & Regulatory Bodies**, and **Delivery & Project Execution Team**.\n\n```\n                           ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n                           │       LIC Market-Driven System          │\n                           └────────────────────┬────────────────────┘\n                                                │\n         ┌──────────────────────┬───────────────┴───────────────┬──────────────────────┐\n         ▼                      ▼                               ▼                      ▼\n┌──────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────┐           ┌──────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────┐\n│ Primary Internal │   │ Primary External │           │  Regulatory &    │   │ Implementation   │\n│   (LIC Staff)    │   │   (End Users)    │           │    Compliance    │   │  (Retinodes/IT)  │\n└──────────────────┘   └──────────────────┘           └──────────────────┘   └──────────────────┘\n```\n\n---\n\n### Group A: Primary Internal Stakeholders (LIC Organization)\n\n#### 1. LIC Executive Management\n* **Role:** Business Sponsors & Strategic Decision Makers.\n* **Key Perspectives & Priorities:** \n  * Increase market share against private competitors.\n  * Maximize profitability and return on investment (ROI).\n  * Ensure strategic alignment of auto-pricing models with business goals.\n* **System Impact:** Relies on high-level analytics, market performance metrics, and reporting dashboards.\n\n#### 2. Insurance Agents & Advisors\n* **Role:** Primary Sales & Distribution Channel.\n* **Key Perspectives & Priorities:** \n  * Streamlined workflow to quickly generate quotes and close sales.\n  * Commission transparency and clear incentive structures.\n  * Access to real-time competition analysis tools to recommend bundled packages.\n* **Potential Conflict:** May resist automated self-service customer features if they perceive a threat to commission structures.\n\n#### 3. Underwriters\n* **Role:** Risk Assessment & Policy Approval Specialists.\n* **Key Perspectives & Priorities:** \n  * Strict adherence to risk guidelines and exposure thresholds.\n  * Automated validation rules for custom packages to reduce manual reviews.\n  * Clear override authority for high-risk or custom-tailored customer requests.\n* **Potential Conflict:** Tends to favor conservative risk profiles, conflicting with Management/Agent desires for aggressive market pricing.\n\n#### 4. Policy Administrators & Operations Team\n* **Role:** Operational Execution, Policy Issuance, & Claims Processing.\n* **Key Perspectives & Priorities:** \n  * Seamless transition from policy creation to active servicing.\n  * Reduction in operational errors, duplicate data entry, and manual processing.\n  * Clear business rules for package renewals, modifications, and cancellations.\n\n#### 5. LIC Internal IT & Infrastructure Team\n* **Role:** Maintenance of Legacy Systems & Enterprise Security.\n* **Key Perspectives & Priorities:** \n  * Smooth API integration with existing backend databases and core banking/payment gateways.\n  * Compliance with enterprise cybersecurity, data protection, and uptime SLAs.\n\n---\n\n### Group B: Primary External Stakeholders\n\n#### 6. End-Customers (Policyholders & Prospects)\n* **Role:** Direct Buyers of Bundled & Custom Insurance Packages.\n* **Key Perspectives & Priorities:** \n  * Intuitive user interface to create custom packages based on personal budget/needs.\n  * Instant feedback, clear pricing, and competitive comparison against market rivals.\n  * Transparency regarding exclusions, terms, and claims procedures.\n* **System Impact:** Primary users of the *Customer-Driven Package Builder* module.\n\n---\n\n### Group C: Regulatory & Governance Stakeholders\n\n#### 7. Insurance Regulatory Authority (e.g., IRDAI)\n* **Role:** Legal and Statutory Governing Body.\n* **Key Perspectives & Priorities:** \n  * Full compliance with statutory pricing caps, non-discriminatory rules, and policy disclosure norms.\n  * Auditability of automated pricing algorithms and customer data usage.\n  * Consumer protection and data privacy mandates.\n\n---\n\n### Group D: Delivery & Implementation Stakeholders (Retinodes & Project Team)\n\n#### 8. Retinodes Requirements Analysis Team\n* **Role:** Elicitation, Negotiation, Modeling, and Validation of Requirements.\n* **Key Perspectives & Priorities:** \n  * Building a repeatable Requirements Engineering framework for market-driven projects.\n  * Resolving conflicting expectations among agents, underwriters, and management.\n\n#### 9. Retinodes Software Development & Architecture Team\n* **Role:** System Design, Coding, & Technical Implementation.\n* **Key Perspectives & Priorities:** \n  * Clear, unambiguous functional specs (SRS) and documented business rules.\n  * System modularity, scalability, and technical feasibility.\n\n#### 10. Retinodes Quality Assurance (QA) Team\n* **Role:** System Validation & Acceptance Testing.\n* **Key Perspectives & Priorities:** \n  * Verifiable, testable functional and non-functional requirements.\n  * Automated test suites for complex package pricing and validation logic.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Stakeholder Power-Interest Matrix (Mendelow's Matrix)\n\nTo prioritize stakeholder engagement during requirements elicitation and negotiation, stakeholders are mapped based on their **Power** (ability to influence project decisions) and **Interest** (level of daily impact by the system):\n\n```\n HIGH POWER\n    ▲\n    │  [ Keep Satisfied ]             │  [ Manage Closely ]\n    │  • Insurance Regulatory Body     │  • LIC Executive Management\n    │  • LIC IT & Security             │  • Underwriters\n    │                                  │  • Insurance Agents\n    ├──────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────\n    │  [ Monitor (Minimum Effort) ]   │  [ Keep Informed ]\n    │  • General Public/Prospects      │  • End-Customers (Policyholders)\n    │                                  │  • Policy Administrators\n    │                                  │  • Development & QA Teams\n    └──────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────► HIGH INTEREST\n LOW POWER\n```\n\n### Engagement Strategy:\n1. **Manage Closely (High Power / High Interest):**  \n   Focus negotiations here. LIC Management, Underwriters, and Insurance Agents have competing priorities (Profitability vs. Risk Control vs. Ease of Sale) that require continuous alignment workshops.\n2. **Keep Satisfied (High Power / Low Interest):**  \n   Ensure strict compliance with Regulatory rules and IT Security standards early in the requirements phase to avoid architectural rework.\n3. **Keep Informed (Low Power / High Interest):**  \n   Gather usability requirements and feedback from End-Customers and Policy Administrators via prototypes, surveys, and UAT sessions.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Immediate Next Steps for Requirements Elicitation\n\n1. **Conduct Joint Application Design (JAD) Sessions:** Facilitate structured workshops with **Agents**, **Underwriters**, and **LIC Management** to reconcile rule engine boundaries for custom package creation.\n2. **Analyze Market Competitor Offerings:** Benchmark existing market packages to establish baseline requirements for the automated consolidated packaging engine.\n3. **Establish Requirement Tracing Framework:** Implement a traceability matrix connecting stakeholder expectations to functional specifications and feasibility reports for the Retinodes development team.", 'extras': {'signature': ''}}]

=== GOALS ===
[{'type': 'text', 'text': 'Based on the provided Stakeholder Identification Report and project context for the **LIC Market-Driven System (MDS)**, here are the primary goals for each identified stakeholder:\n\n---\n\n### **Group A: Primary Internal Stakeholders (LIC Organization)**\n\n#### **1. LIC Executive Management (Business Sponsors)**\n* **Market Expansion:** Increase market share and gain a competitive edge against private insurance competitors.\n* **Financial Return:** Maximize profitability and achieve a high Return on Investment (ROI) from the new system.\n* **Strategic Alignment:** Ensure that automated pricing algorithms and dynamic packaging models strictly align with high-level enterprise business goals and growth targets.\n\n#### **2. Insurance Agents & Advisors (Sales Channel)**\n* **Sales Efficiency:** Streamline workflow to generate policy quotes rapidly and close sales faster.\n* **Commission Protection:** Maintain complete commission transparency and ensure new automated self-service features do not undermine incentive structures.\n* **Competitive Edge:** Access real-time market competitor analysis tools to effectively recommend consolidated/bundled policy packages to clients.\n\n#### **3. Underwriters (Risk Management)**\n* **Risk Control:** Enforce strict adherence to risk management guidelines, policy limits, and exposure thresholds.\n* **Operational Efficiency:** Establish robust, automated validation rules within the system to reduce manual review burdens for standard custom packages.\n* **Governance Authority:** Retain explicit override authority for high-risk, non-standard, or highly customized policy requests.\n\n#### **4. Policy Administrators & Operations Team**\n* **Smooth Lifecycle Management:** Ensure a seamless operational transition from initial policy creation to active servicing and claims processing.\n* **Error Reduction:** Minimize manual data entry, operational overhead, and duplicate processing errors.\n* **Clear Policy Rules:** Maintain automated, explicit business logic for policy package renewals, modifications, updates, and cancellations.\n\n#### **5. LIC Internal IT & Infrastructure Team**\n* **System Integration:** Achieve secure, reliable API integration between the new MDS software, legacy backend databases, and core payment/banking gateways.\n* **Security & Reliability:** Guarantee strict compliance with enterprise cybersecurity policies, data protection standards, and high-availability uptime SLAs.\n\n---\n\n### **Group B: Primary External Stakeholders**\n\n#### **6. End-Customers (Policyholders & Prospects)**\n* **Personalized Coverage:** Use an intuitive, self-service package builder to create custom insurance packages tailored to individual budgets and needs.\n* **Instant Transparency:** Receive immediate pricing calculations, clear feature comparisons against market rivals, and transparent disclosures on exclusions and terms.\n* **Fair Pricing:** Obtain competitive pricing and value-driven package recommendations.\n\n---\n\n### **Group C: Regulatory & Governance Stakeholders**\n\n#### **7. Insurance Regulatory Authority (e.g., IRDAI)**\n* **Statutory Compliance:** Enforce adherence to regulatory pricing caps, non-discriminatory pricing rules, and mandatory policy disclosure guidelines.\n* **Algorithmic Auditability:** Ensure full transparency and auditability of automated pricing algorithms, rule engines, and customer data handling.\n* **Consumer Protection:** Safeguard policyholder data privacy and prevent unfair or misleading policy structures.\n\n---\n\n### **Group D: Delivery & Implementation Stakeholders (Retinodes Team)**\n\n#### **8. Retinodes Requirements Analysis Team**\n* **Framework Establishment:** Develop a repeatable, structured Requirements Engineering framework tailored to market-driven system projects.\n* **Conflict Resolution:** Successfully negotiate and reconcile conflicting requirements between internal factions (e.g., Agents vs. Underwriters vs. Management).\n* **Clear Specifications:** Produce validated, prioritized, and traceable requirement artifacts (SRS, traceability matrix, feasibility report).\n\n#### **9. Retinodes Software Development & Architecture Team**\n* **Technical Feasibility:** Receive unambiguous, documented functional specifications and core business rules.\n* **Architectural Quality:** Build a modular, scalable, maintainable, and robust system architecture capable of managing complex packaging logic.\n\n#### **10. Retinodes Quality Assurance (QA) Team**\n* **Testability:** Ensure all functional and non-functional requirements are verifiable, measurable, and unambiguous.\n* **Quality Automation:** Implement automated test suites to validate complex dynamic pricing models, edge cases, and custom rule-engine boundaries.', 'extras': {'signature': ''}}]

Competitor Analysis & Market Benchmarking** *(Addressing Feedback #1)*\n* **Target Stakeholders:** LIC Executive Management, Retinodes Requirements Team, Insurance Agents.\n* **Justification:** Essential for establishing baseline requirements for the Market-Driven System's *Consolidated Packaging Engine*. By systematically analyzing rival insurance products, pricing models, feature offerings, and dynamic bundling strategies, the team can identify market gaps, competitive feature set requirements, and strategic pricing constraints needed to capture market share.\n\n#### **2. Joint Application Design (JAD) & Negotiation Workshops**\n* **Target Stakeholders:** LIC Executive Management, Underwriters, Insurance Agents, Retinodes Analysis Team.\n* **Justification:** High-power/high-interest internal stakeholders have conflicting priorities (Market Aggressiveness vs. Risk Containment vs. Sales Ease). Semi-Structured Executive & Technical Interviews**\n* **Target Stakeholders:** LIC Executive Management, LIC Internal IT & Infrastructure Team, Underwriting Leads.\n* **Justification:** Enables deep-dive discussions into high-level strategic alignment (ROI targets, market expansion goals) with C-Level executives, while allowing technical leads to define strict non-functional constraints, legacy API integrations, data privacy protocols, and system uptime SLAs.\n\n#### **5. Document Analysis & Regulatory Interface Review**\n* **Target Stakeholders:** Insurance Regulatory Authority (e.g., IRDAI), Policy Administrators, Retinodes QA Team.\n* **Justification:** Critical for extracting explicit regulatory compliance constraints, non-discriminatory pricing mandates, auditability rules, and statutory disclosures directly from legal frameworks and current policy administration guidelines.\n\n#### **6. Interactive Prototyping & Usability Testing**\n* **Target Stakeholders:** End-Customers, Insurance Agents, Policy Administrators.\n* **Justification:** Provides tangible, low/high-fidelity interactive UI mockups of the *Customer-Driven Package Builder* and *Agent Sales Portal*. === FR_NFR ===
[{'type': 'text', 'text': '# Requirements Specification & Feasibility Analysis Report\n**System:** LIC Market-Driven System (MDS)  \n**Author:** Requirements Analysis Team, Retinodes Software Company  \n**Client:** Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)  \n**Document Version:** 2.0 (Final Requirements & Feasibility Baseline)  \n\n---\n\n## 1. Executive Summary & System Overview\n\nThe **LIC Market-Driven System (MDS)** is a strategic digital transformation initiative designed to modernise the agent-insurer relationship, expand LIC’s market share against agile private competitors, and deliver dynamic, customizable insurance packages. \n\nThe system provides two core capabilities:\n1. **Consolidated Packaging Engine (CPE):** A system that continuously ingests competitive intelligence and automatically dynamically bundles life, health, term, and rider policies into pre-packaged, market-competitive solutions.\n2. **Customer-Driven Package Builder (CPB):** A self-service and agent-assisted web application that enables end-customers to construct custom multi-policy packages tailored to individual budgets and coverage needs, featuring instant sub-second price recalculation, real-time risk validation, and automated underwriting triage.\n\nTo resolve channel conflict and operational bottlenecks, MDS incorporates an **Agent Sales & Commission Portal (ASP)** with commission calculation, along with a dedicated **Manual Underwriting Workdesk (UWW)** that handles complex risk reviews, manual loading factors, and risk overrides.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Domain & Regulatory Analysis\n\n### 2.1 Domain Context & Rules\nThe Indian insurance market operates under strict regulations defined by the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)**. MDS enforces these rules at the logic layer:\n* **Statutory Pricing Caps:** Maximum and minimum premium loading limits based on risk bands.\n* **Non-Discriminatory Bundling Rules:** Policy bundles cannot charge a total premium higher than the sum of individual standalone component premiums unless explicit value-added riders are added.\n* **Algorithmic Auditability:** All dynamic pricing, automated package suggestions, and underwriting decision logs must maintain a 10-year immutable audit trail for regulatory inspection.\n\n### 2.2 Competitor Benchmarking Context\nPrivate insurers utilize real-time dynamic quoting tools that offer instant multi-policy volume discounts. MDS integrates a dynamic benchmark engine that ingests, parses, and evaluates top market offerings (e.g., HDFC Life, ICICI Prudential, SBI Life) to generate counter-offers with adjusted premiums, enhanced riders, or higher coverage limits.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Functional Requirements (FRs)\n\n### Module 1: Competitor Benchmarking & Data Management (CBM)\n\n#### `FR-CBM-01`: Competitor Pricing & Feature Data Ingestion\n* **Description:** The system shall ingest, parse, and store market pricing structures, multi-policy discount slabs, rider conditions, and coverage caps from top private competitors.\n* **Inputs:** Automated API feeds, structured batch XML/JSON updates, manual administrative entry forms.\n* **Outputs:** Validated Competitor Benchmark Database records.\n* **Business Logic:** \n  1. Administrative staff or scheduled jobs upload/fetch competitor product structures.\n  2. The system validates schema integrity and updates effective dates.\n  3. Outdated competitor data (>30 days) triggers an administrative alert for review.\n\n#### `FR-CBM-02`: Dynamic Market Gap Analysis Engine\n* **Description:** The system shall calculate market coverage and price deltas between current LIC offerings/packages and rival products.\n* **Inputs:** Proposed LIC Package structure, target demographic profile, Competitor Benchmark Database.\n* **Outputs:** Coverage gap scores, premium differential percentages, and counter-package recommendations.\n* **Business Logic:** \n  1. For any custom or standard package, the system queries rival products matching demographic inputs (age, income band, term length).\n  2. Calculates $\\Delta P = P_{\\text{LIC}} - P_{\\text{Competitor}}$ and identifies feature gaps (e.g., critical illness rider limit differences).\n  3. Generates optimal package tweaks (e.g., "Add Accidental Death Rider for ₹15/mo to match Rival X package value").\n\n#### `FR-CBM-03`: Benchmarked Quote Visualizer\n* **Description:** The system shall present dynamic side-by-side comparison cards to Agents and End-Customers highlighting LIC package advantages over rival offerings.\n* **Inputs:** Selected LIC quote, generated competitor counter-packages.\n* **Outputs:** Visual comparison view (UI widget) displaying pricing, riders, and financial strength metrics.\n* **Business Logic:** Comparisons must conform to IRDAI non-misleading marketing guidelines; disclaimers must automatically attach to exported comparison PDFs.\n\n---\n\n### Module 2: Consolidated Packaging Engine (CPE)\n\n#### `FR-CPE-01`: Multi-Policy Package Aggregation\n* **Description:** The system shall aggregate standalone LIC products (Life, Endowment, Term, Health, Riders) into unified multi-policy packages.\n* **Inputs:** Policy selection inputs, customer risk profile.\n* **Outputs:** Unified package quote with a single consolidated premium schedule.\n* **Business Logic:** Validates mutually exclusive rider combinations (e.g., total term cover cannot exceed statutory ratios relative to base endowment cover).\n\n#### `FR-CPE-02`: Multi-Policy Discount Calculation\n* **Description:** The system shall automatically calculate and apply multi-policy volume discounts based on the number of policies combined in a package.\n* **Inputs:** Un-discounted base premiums of selected component policies.\n* **Outputs:** Discounted total premium breakdown and net savings display.\n* **Business Logic:** Applies discount tiers (e.g., 2 policies = 5% base discount, 3+ policies = 8% base discount), subject to IRDAI maximum allowable discount caps.\n\n---\n\n### Module 3: Customer-Driven Package Builder (CPB)\n\n#### `FR-CPB-01`: Interactive Coverage Builder Interface\n* **Description:** The system shall provide an intuitive self-service builder allowing users to select policies, adjust sum assured sliders, modify policy terms, and toggle optional riders.\n* **Inputs:** User selections via interactive sliders, checkboxes, and budget inputs.\n* **Outputs:** Real-time visual package structure and active policy stack.\n\n#### `FR-CPB-02`: Sub-Second Real-Time Price Recalculation\n* **Description:** The system shall recalculate the total package premium within 1.5 seconds whenever a customer or agent adjusts any coverage slider or rider setting.\n* **Inputs:** Modified policy parameters, dynamic pricing engine state.\n* **Outputs:** Recalculated total premium, tax components, and payment schedule.\n* **Business Logic:** Recalculation calls the core dynamic pricing API asynchronously without requiring full page reloads.\n\n---\n\n### Module 4: Automated Risk & Rules Engine (RUG)\n\n#### `FR-RUG-01`: Automated Risk Validation & Underwriting Triage\n* **Description:** The system shall evaluate custom policy packages against underwriting rules to route them to one of three workflows: Auto-Approved, Loading Factor Required, or Escalated to Manual Underwriting Workdesk.\n* **Inputs:** Customer demographic data, health declarations, sum assured values, package composition.\n* **Outputs:** Underwriting Triage Decision (`AUTO_APPROVE`, `AUTO_LOAD`, `MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED`).\n* **Business Logic:** \n  1. *Auto-Approve:* Sum Assured $\\le$ ₹5,000,000 AND clean medical declaration AND age $\\le$ 45.\n  2. *Auto-Load:* Pre-existing conditions within defined low-risk bands apply automated standard percentage loading (e.g., +10% base rate).\n  3. *Manual Review:* Sum Assured > ₹5,000,000 OR positive high-risk health markers OR custom package combinations exceeding automated risk bounds.\n\n#### `FR-RUG-02`: Regulatory Boundary Enforcer\n* **Description:** The system shall block quote generation if a custom package violates IRDAI statutory rules or pricing caps.\n* **Inputs:** Package configuration, underwriting rules.\n* **Outputs:** Validation Pass signal OR explicit hard-stop regulatory error messages.\n\n---\n\n### Module 5: Manual Underwriting Workdesk & Workflow (UWW)\n\n#### `FR-UWW-01`: Underwriter Task Queue & Case Triage\n* **Description:** The system shall route complex or high-risk custom package applications flagged as `MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED` to a centralized, role-based Underwriter Workdesk task queue.\n* **Inputs:** Flagged quote applications, underwriter authorization level, workdesk workload balance.\n* **Outputs:** Assigned underwriter task list prioritized by risk severity and submission age.\n* **Business Logic:** Routes tasks based on underwriter delegation authority (e.g., Underwriter Level 1: covers up to ₹20M sum assured; Level 2 / Senior Underwriter: covers > ₹20M).\n\n#### `FR-UWW-02`: Manual Risk Evaluation & Custom Loading Factor Entry\n* **Description:** The system shall provide underwriters with an interactive evaluation workspace to review health declarations, financial records, and custom package structures, allowing entry of custom loading factors or exclusion terms.\n* **Inputs:** Medical reports, financial documents, underwriter numeric inputs (custom loading percentage, exclusion codes).\n* **Outputs:** Updated package quote with custom loading rate, revised premium calculation, and updated terms.\n* **Business Logic:** Underwriter enters specific risk loading (e.g., +15% due to occupational hazard). The system immediately updates the package price and regenerates the quote for customer/agent approval.\n\n#### `FR-UWW-03`: Underwriter Decisioning & Override Management\n* **Description:** The system shall allow authorized underwriters to formally Approve, Reject with Reason, or Issue a Counter-Offer for custom packages, with escalation rules for risk overrides exceeding standard parameters.\n* **Inputs:** Underwriter action (`APPROVE`, `REJECT`, `COUNTER_OFFER`), decision notes, escalation flags.\n* **Outputs:** Updated package status notification sent to Agent/Customer portal.\n* **Business Logic:** If an underwriter overrides an automated rule violation (e.g., waiving a standard loading), the system requires secondary approval from a Chief Underwriter if the risk override exceeds ₹50,000 in annual premium impact.\n\n#### `FR-UWW-04`: Underwriter Audit Logging\n* **Description:** The system shall record an unalterable audit entry for every underwriter action, risk loading modification, decision rationale, and approval override.\n* **Inputs:** User ID, timestamp, initial quote parameters, modified parameters, underwriter justification text.\n* **Outputs:** Immutable audit log entry stored in the compliance database.\n\n---\n\n### Module 6: Agent Sales & Commission Portal (ASP)\n\n#### `FR-ASP-01`: Agent Commission Transparency Engine\n* **Description:** The system shall calculate real-time commission breakdowns for agents selling automated or custom multi-policy packages, preventing sales channel resistance.\n* **Inputs:** Package components, agent tier, commission model rules.\n* **Outputs:** Projected commission display (upfront + renewal breakdown per package).\n* **Business Logic:** Ensures split-commission models for multi-policy packages are explicitly itemized per component policy.\n\n#### `FR-ASP-02`: Agent Time-to-Quote Workflow Execution\n* **Description:** The system shall enable agents to convert custom customer builder configurations into official binding quotes in under 3 minutes, exporting quote summaries via SMS, email, or WhatsApp link.\n* **Inputs:** Customer package configuration ID, agent authorization token.\n* **Outputs:** Official quote document (PDF) and deep-link payment portal URL.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs)\n\n### 4.1 Performance & Scalability\n* `NFR-PERF-01` **Latency / Real-Time Recalculation:** The system shall complete dynamic package premium recalculations (`FR-CPB-02`) in $\\le 1.5 \\text{ seconds}$ under a concurrent load of up to 10,000 users.\n\n### 4.2 Security & Data Protection\n* `NFR-SEC-01` **Cybersecurity & Encryption Standard:** All data in transit must be encrypted using TLS 1.3, and all sensitive customer health and financial data at rest must be encrypted using AES-256. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) must govern access to the Underwriting Workdesk.\n\n### 4.3 Reliability & Availability\n* `NFR-AVAIL-01` **System Availability & Uptime:** The system shall maintain 99.95% operational availability during core business hours (06:00 to 22:00 IST), with planned maintenance restricted to off-peak hours.\n\n### 4.4 System Integration & APIs\n* `NFR-INT-01` **Backend API & Legacy Integration SLA:** All API interfaces connecting MDS with LIC legacy core policy administration systems shall respond within $800 \\text{ ms}$, implementing circuit breaker patterns to prevent cascading failures if legacy systems degrade.\n\n### 4.5 Compliance & Auditability\n* `NFR-COMP-01` **Regulatory Audit Logging:** The system shall store audit trails for dynamic pricing, competitor comparisons, and underwriter overrides (`FR-UWW-04`) for a minimum of 10 years in compliance with IRDAI rules.\n\n### 4.6 Usability & UX\n* `NFR-USA-01` **Agent Task Efficiency:** Field agents shall be able to complete a multi-policy quote generation task within $\\le 3 \\text{ minutes}$ on mobile and tablet devices.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM)\n\n| Requirement ID | Requirement Description | Target Stakeholder Group | Primary Stakeholder Goal | Traceable Architectural Component | Verification Method |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **`FR-CBM-01`** | Competitor Data Ingestion | Executive Management / Retinodes | Market Expansion / Strategic Alignment | Competitor Data Service | Microservices              │ High. JAD workshops               │ High. Target ROI │\n│ architecture & REST              │ resolved agent commission         │ expected within  │\n│ adapters bridge                  │ fears and standardized            │ 12 months via    │\n│ legacy backends cleanly.         │ underwriter escalation queues.    │ cross-sell lift. │\n└──────────────────┘               └──────────────────┘               └──────────────────┘\n```\n\n1. **Technical Feasibility:** **HIGH**. The microservices architecture separates dynamic recalculation engines from legacy backend databases. RESTful API wrappers and caching buffers ensure sub-second response times (`NFR-PERF-01`) without overloading core backend infrastructure.\n2. **Operational Feasibility:** **HIGH**. JAD negotiation workshops successfully aligned incentives: commission transparency (`FR-ASP-01`) prevents agent channel resistance, while clear delegation bounds (`FR-UWW-01` to `FR-UWW-03`) maintain underwriter risk authority.\n3. **Economic Feasibility:** **HIGH**. Market analysis indicates cross-selling consolidated packages increases policy size per customer by 22–30%. Project development costs will be offset within 12 months post-launch through increased market share and reduced manual underwriting overhead.\n\n---\n\n### 6.2 MoSCoW Prioritization Matrix\n\n| Category | Requirement IDs & Key Features | Rationale / Business Justification |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **Must Have** | `FR-CPE-01`, `FR-CPB-01`, `FR-CPB-02`, `FR-RUG-01`, `FR-RUG-02`, `FR-UWW-01`, `FR-UWW-02`, `FR-ASP-01`, `NFR-PERF-01`, `NFR-SEC-01`, `NFR-AVAIL-01`, `NFR-INT-01` | Non-negotiable core functionality required to package policies, perform automated/manual underwriting, compute real-time quotes, compensate agents, and meet regulatory security standards. |\n| **Should Have** | `FR-CBM-01`, `FR-CBM-02`, `FR-CBM-03`, `FR-UWW-03`, `FR-UWW-04`, `FR-ASP-02`, `NFR-COMP-01`, `NFR-USA-01` | Critical for competitive positioning, formal underwriting escalation management, audit compliance, and achieving market superiority over rival insurers. |\n| **Could Have** | `FR-CPE-02` (Advanced multi-tier dynamic discount algorithms beyond standard volume caps), AI-driven package recommendations. | Enhances user experience and optimization, but standard static discount rules can serve as an interim solution for launch. |\n| **Won\'t Have (This Release)** | Fully automated direct-to-consumer medical underwriter bypass for high-risk profiles (>₹20M sum assured). | High risk of regulatory rejection and financial loss; strict manual underwriter review must be retained for V1 launch. |', 'extras': {'signature': ''}}]
